public_rationale: Part of the claim holds. The UN transcript shows Bengio, Altman, Amodei and Delangue all calling for model testing or evaluation, transparency or incident reporting, and international cooperation. Many states said similar things. But 'pretty much everyone converged on exactly the same things' goes too far. Liability appears in the remarks of Bengio, France and Liberia, but not in Altman's or Amodei's, even though Marcus counts the CEOs in the consensus. And the US speaker, Michael Kratsios, rejected new global governance structures and said rapid progress was 'not a reason to pause' AI. That is open dissent on international cooperation and immediate action.
limitations: The transcript is automated and not the official record.
'Pretty much everyone' is vague, so how much dissent the claim allows is a judgment call.
Finding no liability mention depends on keyword searches of an automated transcript.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nearly all speakers at the UN Security Council AI briefing, including Altman and Amodei, agreed on the policy measures Marcus has long called for.

statement.excerpt: Pretty much everyone converged on exactly the same things I keep harping on:
statement.document_title: Historic UN Security Council Briefing on AI

from_speaker: exactly the same things I keep harping on
our_interpretation: Read 'pretty much everyone' as nearly all speakers at the 23 September 2026 Security Council AI briefing: the four briefers (Bengio, Altman, Amodei, Delangue) and most member-state speakers.

Read 'converged on exactly the same things' as nearly all speakers backing all five listed measures, or at least not opposing them. The post says the CEOs were part of the consensus, so Altman's and Amodei's speeches are central.
Plain reading: the claim fails if a major speaker openly rejected one of the listed measures, or if the CEOs left out a listed measure such as liability.
criteria.support_condition: The meeting record shows nearly all speakers, including Altman and Amodei, calling for pre-deployment testing, transparency or audits, liability, international cooperation and urgent action, with no major speaker dissenting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The record shows a major speaker rejecting one of the measures (for example, international governance), or shows the CEOs not endorsing a listed measure such as liability.
